Interior design spec sheet template

A specification sheet records what an item is meant to be. It should let someone distinguish the proposed product, finish, size, and revision without inferring those details from an image.

What each field records

Reference
Stable ID carried into plans and schedules.
Selection
A proposed product or clearly labeled concept.
Application
Where the item is used.
Dimensions / unit
State all relevant dimensions and units; leave unknowns explicit.
Material / finish
Name the finish and sample reference if verified.
Supplier / model
Record a verified supplier and model before order approval.
Source / quote date
Identify the source and date for supplied product information.
Status
Distinguish proposed, pending review, and approved.
Revision
Identify the current issue.
Review note
Record unresolved dimensions, suitability, and coordination.

How to use this template

Use the sheet for product-level information. Keep the FF&E schedule as the room-by-room quantity register and the finish schedule as the surface register. Terminology varies between practices; agree the role of each document with the people using it.

  1. Assign a reference before adding the item to a drawing.
  2. Record sourced information separately from assumptions.
  3. Review the specification alongside its room schedule and drawings before any purchasing decision.

Review before use

  • An image is not proof of model, dimensions, or finish.
  • Do not overwrite a revision without recording the change.
  • Do not label an item approved because it appears in a concept board.
